verdict.rationale: Kong's own repo documents advanced routing, load balancing and health checking, configurable via the Admin API or declarative config. It also documents plugins for request/response transformations, so all three parts of the story are covered first-party. A community issue reports an intermittent router-cache 404 bug on the old 0.14.1 release, which is a version-specific defect rather than a contradiction of the capability. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on load-balancing algorithms and the transformation plugins (evidence is README-level one-liners), and independent hands-on corroboration on current versions.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can route, load-balance, and transform requests between consumers and upstream services

citations.quote: Advanced routing, load balancing, health checking - all configurable via a RESTful admin API or declarative configuration.
Plugins for enforcing traffic controls, rate limiting, req/res transformations, logging, monitoring
By providing functionality for proxying, routing, load balancing, health checking, authentication (and more), Kong serves as the central layer for orchestrating microservices
